body.en: Rational functions are quotients of polynomial functions whose graphs exhibit rich asymptotic behaviors, poles, and removable singularities. Analyzing rational functions provides the conceptual and technical foundation for differential and integral calculus — including limits, continuity, asymptotes, and partial fraction decomposition.
body.ar: Rational الدوال are quotients of كثيرة الحدود الدوال whose graphs exhibit rich asymptotic behaviors, poles, and removable singularities. Analyzing rational الدوال provides the conceptual and technical foundation for differential and التكامل التفاضل والتكامل — including النهايات, continuity, خطوط التقارب, and partial fraction decomposition.

label.ar: ● Natural المجال, Holes & Vertical خطوط التقارب

body.en:
For a rational function \(R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are polynomials:

  • Natural Domain: \(\mathcal{D} = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid q(x) \ne 0\}\).
  • Removable Discontinuity (Hole): If \((x - c)\) is a factor of both \(p(x)\) and \(q(x)\) with multiplicity \(m_p \ge m_q\), the graph possesses a hole at \((c, L)\), where \(L = \lim_{x \to c} R(x)\).
  • Vertical Asymptote (Pole): If \(q(c) = 0\) while \(p(c) \ne 0\) (or \(m_q > m_p\)), the line \(x = c\) is a vertical asymptote: \[ \lim_{x \to c^-} R(x) = \pm\infty \quad \text{and/or} \quad \lim_{x \to c^+} R(x) = \pm\infty. \]
body.ar:
For a rational الدالة \(R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\) حيث \(p\) and \(q\) are polynomials:

  • Natural المجال: \(\mathcal{D} = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid q(x) \ne 0\}\).
  • Removable Discontinuity (Hole): If \((x - c)\) is a factor of both \(p(x)\) and \(q(x)\) with multiplicity \(m_p \ge m_q\), the التمثيل البياني possesses a hole at \((c, L)\), حيث \(L = \lim_{x \to c} R(x)\).
  • Vertical خط التقارب (Pole): If \(q(c) = 0\) while \(p(c) \ne 0\) (or \(m_q > m_p\)), the line \(x = c\) is a vertical خط التقارب: \[ \lim_{x \to c^-} R(x) = \pm\infty \quad \text{and/or} \quad \lim_{x \to c^+} R(x) = \pm\infty. \]

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Rational Functions, Limits & Continuity)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Rational الدوال, النهايات & Continuity)

body.en:
Why Differentiability Implies Continuity & How Implicit Differentiation Works: Notice that for \(x \ne a\), we can write \(f(x) - f(a) = \dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\cdot (x - a)\). Taking the limit as \(x \to a\) by the Product Law gives:

\[ \lim_{x \to a} \bigl(f(x) - f(a)\bigr) = f'(a)\cdot 0 = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a) \]

Similarly, when differentiating an implicit relation \(F(x, y) = c\) with respect to \(x\), \(y = y(x)\) is an inner function of \(x\). By the Chain Rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[y^n\bigr] = ny^{n-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), and for product terms \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[xy] = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

problem.en: Perform a complete analysis of \(f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 8}{x^2 - x - 6}\). Identify domain, zeros, holes, vertical asymptotes, horizontal asymptotes, and \(y\)-intercept.
problem.ar: Perform a complete analysis of \(f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 8}{x^2 - x - 6}\). Identify المجال, zeros, holes, vertical خطوط التقارب, horizontal خطوط التقارب, and \(y\)-المقطع.

solution.en:
Step 1: Factor numerator and denominator: \[ f(x) = \frac{2(x^2 - 4)}{(x - 3)(x + 2)} = \frac{2(x - 2)(x + 2)}{(x - 3)(x + 2)}. \]

Step 2: Natural Domain: Denominator roots are \(x = 3\) and \(x = -2\). \[ \mathcal{D} = (-\infty, -2) \cup (-2, 3) \cup (3, \infty). \]

Step 3: Removable hole: The factor \((x + 2)\) cancels for all \(x \ne -2\). The reduced function is \(g(x) = \frac{2(x - 2)}{x - 3}\). Evaluating at \(x = -2\): \[ g(-2) = \frac{2(-2 - 2)}{-2 - 3} = \frac{2(-4)}{-5} = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6 \implies \text{Hole at } (-2, 1.6). \]

Step 4: Asymptotes and intercepts:

  • Vertical Asymptote: The uncancelled denominator root is \(x = 3\).
  • Horizontal Asymptote: Degrees are equal (\(n = d = 2\)), so \(y = \frac{2}{1} = 2\).
  • \(x\)-intercept: Uncancelled numerator root: \(x - 2 = 0 \implies (2, 0)\).
  • \(y\)-intercept: \(f(0) = \frac{-8}{-6} = \frac{4}{3} \implies (0, 4/3)\).

Step 4: خطوط التقارب and intercepts:

  • Vertical خط التقارب: The uncancelled denominator root is \(x = 3\).

label.ar: ● Slant (Oblique) خطوط التقارب & خط التقارب Crossing مبرهنة

body.en:
When \(\deg(p) = \deg(q) + 1\), perform polynomial long division: \[ R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)} = (mx + b) + \frac{r(x)}{q(x)}, \quad \text{where } \deg(r) < \deg(q). \] As \(x \to \pm\infty\), \(\frac{r(x)}{q(x)} \to 0\), establishing the slant asymptote \(y = mx + b\).

Intersection Principle: While a function can never cross a vertical asymptote, it can intersect its horizontal or slant asymptote at finite points. Solve \(R(x) = y_{\text{asymptote}} \iff r(x) = 0\) to locate all intersection coordinates.
body.ar:
When \(\deg(p) = \deg(q) + 1\), perform كثيرة الحدود long division: \[ R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)} = (mx + b) + \frac{r(x)}{q(x)}, \quad \text{where } \deg(r) < \deg(q). \] As \(x \to \pm\infty\), \(\frac{r(x)}{q(x)} \to 0\), establishing the slant خط التقارب \(y = mx + b\).

Intersection Principle: While a الدالة can never cross a vertical خط التقارب, it can intersect its horizontal or slant خط التقارب at finite points. Solve \(R(x) = y_{\text{asymptote}} \iff r(x) = 0\) to locate all التقاطع الإحداثيات.

label.en: ● Complete Taxonomy of Graphs of Continuity & The 3-Part Checklist
label.ar: ● Complete Taxonomy of Graphs of Continuity & The 3-Part Checklist (الدوال النسبية والنهايات والاتصال)

body.en:
A function \(f\) is continuous at \(x = c\) if and only if all three conditions of the Continuity Checklist hold: (1) \(f(c)\) is defined; (2) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x)\) exists (finite left & right limits agree); (3) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = f(c)\).

The six geometric cases of continuity and discontinuity graphs are:

  • Case 1 · Continuous: All 3 conditions pass. The curve is unbroken at \(x = c\).
  • Case 2 · Removable (Hole): \(f(c)\) undefined, but limit exists. An open circle appears at \((c, L)\).
  • Case 3 · Removable (Displaced Point): \(f(c) \neq L\); an open circle at \((c, L)\) and an isolated dot at \((c, f(c))\).
  • Case 4 · Jump Discontinuity: Left and right limits are finite but unequal.
  • Case 5 · Infinite Discontinuity (Vertical Asymptote): Function values grow without bound to \(\pm\infty\).
  • Case 6 · Oscillating Discontinuity: Function oscillates infinitely often as \(x \to c\); limit does not exist.
body.ar:
A الدالة \(f\) is continuous at \(x = c\) if and only if all three conditions of the Continuity Checklist hold: (1) \(f(c)\) is defined; (2) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x)\) exists (finite left & right النهايات agree); (3) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = f(c)\).

The six geometric cases of continuity and discontinuity graphs are:

  • Case 1 · Continuous: All 3 conditions pass. The curve is unbroken at \(x = c\).
  • Case 2 · Removable (Hole): \(f(c)\) undefined, but النهاية exists. An open الدائرة appears at \((c, L)\).
  • Case 3 · Removable (Displaced Point): \(f(c) \neq L\); an open الدائرة at \((c, L)\) and an isolated dot at \((c, f(c))\).
  • Case 4 · Jump Discontinuity: Left and right النهايات are finite but unequal.
  • Case 5 · Infinite Discontinuity (Vertical خط التقارب): الدالة values grow without bound to \(\pm\infty\).
  • Case 6 · Oscillating Discontinuity: الدالة oscillates infinitely often as \(x \to c\); النهاية does not exist.

problem.en: Determine the slant asymptote of \(f(x) = \frac{2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5}{x^2 + 1}\) and find the exact coordinates of any point where the curve intersects its asymptote.
problem.ar: حدّد slant خط التقارب of \(f(x) = \frac{2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5}{x^2 + 1}\) and أوجد exact الإحداثيات of any point حيث the curve intersects its خط التقارب.

solution.en:
Step 1: Perform polynomial long division: \[ \begin{array}{r} 2x - 3 \phantom{)} \\ x^2 + 1{\overline{\smash{\big)}\,2x^3 - 3x^2 + 0x + 5}} \\ \underline{-(2x^3 + 0x^2 + 2x)\phantom{-5}} \\ -3x^2 - 2x + 5 \\ \underline{-(-3x^2 + 0x - 3)} \\ -2x + 8 \end{array} \] Thus, \(f(x) = (2x - 3) + \frac{-2x + 8}{x^2 + 1}\). The slant asymptote is \(y = 2x - 3\).

Step 2: Find intersection point: Set the remainder term equal to zero: \[ \frac{-2x + 8}{x^2 + 1} = 0 \implies -2x + 8 = 0 \implies x = 4. \] Substitute \(x = 4\) into the asymptote equation: \[ y = 2(4) - 3 = 8 - 3 = 5. \] The curve intersects its slant asymptote at the point \((4, 5)\).
solution.ar:
Step 1: Perform كثيرة الحدود long division: \[ \begin{array}{r} 2x - 3 \phantom{)} \\ x^2 + 1{\overline{\smash{\big)}\,2x^3 - 3x^2 + 0x + 5}} \\ \underline{-(2x^3 + 0x^2 + 2x)\phantom{-5}} \\ -3x^2 - 2x + 5 \\ \underline{-(-3x^2 + 0x - 3)} \\ -2x + 8 \end{array} \] وعليه, \(f(x) = (2x - 3) + \frac{-2x + 8}{x^2 + 1}\). The slant خط التقارب is \(y = 2x - 3\).

Step 2: Find التقاطع point: Set the remainder term equal to zero: \[ \frac{-2x + 8}{x^2 + 1} = 0 \implies -2x + 8 = 0 \implies x = 4. \] عوّض \(x = 4\) into the خط التقارب المعادلة: \[ y = 2(4) - 3 = 8 - 3 = 5. \] The curve intersects its slant خط التقارب at the point \((4, 5)\).

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced / University Rigor — Partial Fraction Decomposition & Epsilon-Delta Limits

body.en: Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions across distinct linear, repeated linear, and irreducible quadratic factors, and construct formal epsilon-delta limit proofs.
body.ar: Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions across distinct linear, repeated linear, and irreducible quadratic factors, and construct formal epsilon-delta النهاية proofs.

body.en:
Theorem: Any strictly proper rational function \(\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\) (\(\deg p < \deg q\)) decomposes uniquely into a sum of partial fractions governed by the factorization of \(q(x)\) over \(\mathbb{R}\):

  • Distinct Linear Factor \((ax + b)\): Contributes a term \(\frac{A}{ax + b}\).
  • Repeated Linear Factor \((ax + b)^k\): Contributes \(\frac{A_1}{ax + b} + \frac{A_2}{(ax + b)^2} + \dots + \frac{A_k}{(ax + b)^k}\).
  • Irreducible Quadratic Factor \((ax^2 + bx + c)\): Contributes \(\frac{Ax + B}{ax^2 + bx + c}\).

Heaviside Cover-Up Method: For distinct linear factors, the coefficient \(A_i\) of \(\frac{A_i}{x - c_i}\) is obtained instantly by multiplying by \((x - c_i)\) and evaluating at \(x = c_i\): \[ A_i = \lim_{x \to c_i} (x - c_i) \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}. \]
body.ar:
Theorem: Any strictly proper rational الدالة \(\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\) (\(\deg p < \deg q\)) decomposes uniquely into a sum of partial fractions governed by the factorization of \(q(x)\) over \(\mathbb{R}\):

  • Distinct Linear Factor \((ax + b)\): Contributes a term \(\frac{A}{ax + b}\).
  • Repeated Linear Factor \((ax + b)^k\): Contributes \(\frac{A_1}{ax + b} + \frac{A_2}{(ax + b)^2} + \dots + \frac{A_k}{(ax + b)^k}\).
  • Irreducible Quadratic Factor \((ax^2 + bx + c)\): Contributes \(\frac{Ax + B}{ax^2 + bx + c}\).

Heaviside Cover-Up Method: For distinct linear factors, the المعامل \(A_i\) of \(\frac{A_i}{x - c_i}\) is obtained instantly by multiplying by \((x - c_i)\) and evaluating at \(x = c_i\): \[ A_i = \lim_{x \to c_i} (x - c_i) \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}. \]

label.en: ● Precise \((\varepsilon, \delta)\) Definition of Limit & Rigorous Proofs
label.ar: ● Precise \((\varepsilon, \delta)\) تعريف of النهاية & Rigorous Proofs

body.en:
Definition: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L\) means \(\forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists \delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - c| < \delta \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon\).

Proof (Linear Limit): Prove \(\lim_{x\to 3}(4x - 5) = 7\).
Given \(\varepsilon > 0\), choose \(\delta = \frac{\varepsilon}{4}\). If \(0 < |x - 3| < \delta\), then \(|(4x - 5) - 7| = 4|x - 3| < 4\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right) = \varepsilon\). \(\blacksquare\)

Proof (Quadratic with Bounding): Prove \(\lim_{x\to 2} x^2 = 4\).
We factor \(|x^2 - 4| = |x - 2||x + 2|\). Constrain \(\delta \le 1 \implies |x - 2| < 1 \implies 1 < x < 3 \implies |x + 2| < 5\). Choose \(\delta = \min(1, \varepsilon / 5)\). If \(0 < |x - 2| < \delta\), then \(|x^2 - 4| < 5|x - 2| < 5(\varepsilon / 5) = \varepsilon\). \(\blacksquare\)

Proof (Linear النهاية): Prove \(\lim_{x\to 3}(4x - 5) = 7\).

problem.en: Decompose the rational expression \(\frac{5x^2 - 2x + 9}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 4)}\) into its partial fraction components.
problem.ar: Decompose the rational العبارة الجبرية \(\frac{5x^2 - 2x + 9}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 4)}\) into its partial fraction components.

solution.en:
Step 1: Set up the partial fraction template: \[ \frac{5x^2 - 2x + 9}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 4)} = \frac{A}{x - 1} + \frac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 4}. \]

Step 2: Clear denominators: \[ 5x^2 - 2x + 9 = A(x^2 + 4) + (Bx + C)(x - 1). \]

Step 3: Solve for \(A\) using Heaviside substitution (\(x = 1\)): \[ 5(1)^2 - 2(1) + 9 = A(1 + 4) + 0 \implies 12 = 5A \implies A = \frac{12}{5} \implies \text{Let's check arithmetic: } 5 - 2 + 9 = 12. \] Let's verify coefficients directly by equating powers of \(x\): \[ 5x^2 - 2x + 9 = (A + B)x^2 + (-B + C)x + (4A - C). \] System of linear equations:

  1. \(A + B = 5\)

body.en:
• Holes vs. Vertical Asymptotes: A factor \((x - c)\) that cancels completely from both numerator and denominator produces a removable discontinuity (hole) at \((c, g(c))\), where \(g(x)\) is the simplified function. Denominator roots that remain after canceling yield true vertical asymptotes.
  • Asymptote Crossing: A curve can never intersect a vertical asymptote (the function is strictly undefined there). However, a rational curve can intersect its horizontal or slant asymptote at finite values of \(x\). Set \(f(x) = y_{\text{asymptote}}\) to locate intersection coordinates.
  • Slant Asymptote Existence: A slant (oblique) asymptote exists if and only if the degree of the numerator is exactly 1 higher than the denominator (\(\deg p = \deg q + 1\)). The asymptote equation \(y = mx + b\) is the quotient polynomial from long division, ignoring the remainder.
  • Rational Inequality Sign Charts: Never multiply both sides of a rational inequality by a variable denominator expression (e.g. \(x - 2\)) because its sign is undetermined. Move all terms to one side to compare with 0, find all partition points (zeros of numerator and denominator), and test intervals on a sign chart.

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Consider the rational function \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \). What is the value of \( f(x) \) as \( x \) approaches 3?

Step-by-Step Solution: The function is given by \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \). We can factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \( x^2 - 9 = (x-3)(x+3) \). Thus, for \( x \neq 3 \), we can simplify the function to \( f(x) = \dfrac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x - 3} = x + 3 \). To find the limit as \( x \) approaches 3, we can substitute 3 into the simplified expression: \( \lim_{x\to 3} f(x) = \lim_{x\to 3} (x+3) = 3 + 3 = 6 \). Although the function is undefined at \( x=3 \), the limit exists and is 6. Therefore, as \( x \) approaches 3, \( f(x) \) approaches 6.

question.en: Find all vertical and horizontal asymptotes, the exact coordinates of any holes, and all intercepts of the rational function \(R(x) = \dfrac{2x^2 + 5x - 3}{x^2 + 4x + 3}\).

solution.en:

question.en: Determine the slant asymptote of \(g(x) = \dfrac{2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5}{x^2 + 1}\) and find the coordinates of any point where the curve intersects this asymptote.
question.ar: حدّد slant asymptote of \(g(x) = \dfrac{2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5}{x^2 + 1}\) and أوجد إحداثيات any point حيث the curve intersects this asymptote.

solution.en:
Since \(\deg(\text{num}) = 3\) and \(\deg(\text{denom}) = 2\) with \(3 - 2 = 1\), a slant asymptote exists. Perform polynomial long division:

\[(2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5) \div (x^2 + 1) = (2x - 3) + \frac{-2x + 8}{x^2 + 1}.\]

The linear quotient gives the slant asymptote: \(y = 2x - 3\).

To find where the graph intersects this asymptote, set the remainder equal to zero:

\[\frac{-2x + 8}{x^2 + 1} = 0 \implies -2x + 8 = 0 \implies x = 4.\]

Substitute \(x = 4\) into the asymptote equation:

\[y = 2(4) - 3 = 5.\]

The curve intersects its slant asymptote at the point \((4, 5)\).

As \(x \to -2^-\), the numerator approaches \((-2)^2 + 2(-2) + 4 = 4 - 4 + 4 = 4\). The denominator \(x+2\) approaches 0 from the negative side (e.g., if \(x=-2.1\), \(x+2 = -0.1\)). Therefore, the limit is of the form \(\frac{4}{0^-}\), which tends to \(-\infty\).

So, the limit at \(a\) is 3, and \(\lim_{x \to b^-} f(x) = -\infty\). This corresponds to the first choice.

First, we حلّل the numerator and the denominator of \(f(x) = \frac{x^3 - 8}{x^2 - 4}\). The numerator is a dإذا كانference of cubes: \(x^3 - 8 = (x-2)(x^2 + 2x + 4)\). The denominator is a dإذا كانference of squares: \(x^2 - 4 = (x-2)(x+2)\). وعليه، \(f(x) = \frac{(x-2)(x^2 + 2x + 4)}{(x-2)(x+2)}\).

A removable discontinuity occurs حيث a حلّل cancels out. Here, \((x-2)\) cancels, so the removable discontinuity is at \(x=a=2\). To أوجد limit as \(x\) approaches \(a\), we consider the simplإذا كانied function for \(x

question.en: Consider the rational function \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \). What is the value of \( f(x) \) as \( x \) approaches 3?
question.ar: Consider the rational function \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \). ما قيمة \( f(x) \) as \( x \) approaches 3?

hints.en: The function is given by \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: We can factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \( x^2 - 9 = (x-3)(x+3) \). Thus, for \( x eq 3 \), we can simplify the function to \( f(x) = \dfrac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x - 3} = x + 3 \).

solution.en: The function is given by \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \). We can factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \( x^2 - 9 = (x-3)(x+3) \). Thus, for \( x \neq 3 \), we can simplify the function to \( f(x) = \dfrac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x - 3} = x + 3 \). To find the limit as \( x \) approaches 3, we can substitute 3 into the simplified expression: \( \lim_{x\to 3} f(x) = \lim_{x\to 3} (x+3) = 3 + 3 = 6 \). Although the function is undefined at \( x=3 \), the limit exists and is 6. Therefore, as \( x \) approaches 3, \( f(x) \) approaches 6.

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:
